_README: Hand-maintained exceptions for what PSN's API cannot express.
WHY THIS EXISTS. A cross-play trophy set lists every platform a game shipped on and
never says which you own. The sync therefore offers all of them, because absence of
evidence is not evidence of absence: PSN reports play data only for PS4 and later,
so a PS3 or Vita copy can never be confirmed or denied from the feeds. Over-offering
costs a row you delete; under-offering costs a completion with nowhere to attach.
TWO INDEPENDENT AXES, both of which break that default:
shared_trophies=false — each platform had its OWN trophy list. The set you hold
therefore belongs to a single platform, and Sony's multi-platform declaration on
it is noise. Axiom Verge and Bastion are this: one Vita/PS4 string, two real lists.
cross_buy=false — each platform was a separate purchase. Owning the PS4 version
implies nothing about Vita. Dragon's Crown and Trails of Cold Steel are this:
one genuinely shared list, three separate transactions.
ONLY cross_buy=false restricts a default. Ownership is the criterion for putting a row
in the library, and separate trophy lists do not make you own the game less — Axiom
Verge and Bastion have per-platform lists AND cross-buy. shared_trophies is recorded
because it decides which entry the trophy data describes (#136), never to suppress one.
shown on the row. Never silently dropped — a wrong entry here suppresses a platform
the user may own, which is the expensive error, so it has to be visible and fixable.
null means unknown and changes nothing.
MATCHING: `npcomm` (npCommunicationId, e.g. NPWR06670_00) is exact and preferred.
`title` falls back to backend/titles.py's normalizer, so casing, TM/(R), subtitles and
edition suffixes need not be reproduced exactly.
VERIFY BEFORE ADDING. Entries whose claims could not be confirmed live in `_unverified`,
which the loader ignores entirely.
SOURCES: vitaplayer.co.uk/playstation-vita-ps3-ps4-cross-buy-guide (382 titles, EU list,
as of 2024-07-07). Cross-buy was a publisher decision far more often than a regional
one, so the EU list holds for the Americas in the large majority of cases. It only
ever REINFORCES the permissive default; the inverse inference is NOT safe and unused.
REGION. Cross-buy was usually a publisher decision, so the EU and NA lists agree for
the large majority. The known exceptions are Sony's late PS2-collection Vita ports —
the Ratchet & Clank, Jak and Daxter and Sly trilogies — which were cross-buy in EU and
not in North America. Those carry cross_buy=false here, which beats the bulk list.
Entries whose behaviour differs by region say REGIONAL in their notes; this file is
currently written from a North American perspective.

_source: Union of two lists. Both only ever CONFIRM cross-buy, never restrict, so merging is
safe and maximises coverage — a title on either is confirmed.
_note: Used ONLY to reinforce the permissive default and upgrade a row's stated reason from
assumption to fact. An entry in `titles` with cross_buy=false wins over this list.
The two lists broadly agree where they overlap. Their size difference (382 vs 154) is
list completeness, not regional divergence: cross-buy was overwhelmingly a publisher
decision rather than a storefront one, so EU and the Americas matched for the large
majority of titles. A handful of EU-favourable exceptions are believed to exist, which
is why both are kept and neither is treated as authoritative alone.
The inverse — 'absent from this list therefore not cross-buy' — is NOT safe and is not
used anywhere. The EU source is a VITA guide, so PS3/PS4 pairs with no Vita version
(Resident Evil) were never in scope, and the site notes it shrinks as titles delist.
